role: A dependency-free JSON reader for the oracle's tapes and snapshots (values keep their raw text so canonical NBT members feed nbt_parse directly, and canonical "i:"/"f:"/"d:" scalars decode to ints and raw float bits), a growing line reader over FILE or gzFile, and the tape header-then-rows loop.

structs.name: struct tape
structs.java: the oracle's tape format (header line, one JSON row per tick) written by the netherite.oracle recorder

gpu: line 128, function parse_value: recursive descent over nested objects and arrays (recursion depth follows the input)
lines 120, 140-173, functions new_value and parse_value: one malloc per value plus realloc-grown field and item arrays (a pointer tree per parsed row)
line 392, function lines_next: doubles the line buffer with realloc for a long line
line 443, function tape_next: allocates a copy of every row and parses it
notes: Not a port of any Java file: it reads what the oracle (oracle/harness/netherite/oracle) writes. Used by the replay, the tests, dev ops and the renderer's tape-driven paths, outside the simulated tick; a GPU tick would get its inputs from here, host side. Possible leak seen while reading: tape_next (line 452) overwrites t->row without json_free of the previous row, and tape_close frees only the last one; test_snapshots.c's loop does not free rows itself. tape_open's failure paths after fopen also leave the line buffer allocated. Not verified by running anything. json_int truncates a J_NUM through double, so integers above 2^53 lose precision.
